title: Airflow progressive slowness
body: We run Airflow 2.5.3 on EKS with KubernetesExecutor and PostgreSQL metadata. Over 2-3 weeks, executor running-task metrics steadily increase while open slots decrease, until DAG tasks remain queued and no worker pods start. The UI, database, pod logs, CPU, and memory look healthy and show no tasks running. Debug logging shows successfully completed task instances from days earlier still present in the executor's in-memory `self.running` set. Disabling DAGs and marking tasks successful does not recover scheduling, but restarting the scheduler pod resets the metrics and tasks begin executing again. This affects different DAGs and both manual and scheduled runs, and we have not found a reliable reproduction.

symptoms_visible: Over 2-3 weeks, executor running tasks gradually increase and open slots decrease until DAG tasks stay queued and no worker pods start.
The UI and PostgreSQL database show no tasks running, but debug output still lists task instances that completed successfully days ago in `self.running`.
Restarting the scheduler pod resets the executor metrics and tasks start executing again.
N0.label: N0 progressive executor-slot exhaustion reported

symptoms_visible: After Airflow 2.6.3 had been in production for about a week, the running-task count began creeping upward and open slots began falling again.
N1_x.label: N1_x version-upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: The executor slot count still degrades sporadically, and completed task instances are no longer in the database running state by the time I inspect them.
N2.label: N2 task logs compared

symptoms_visible: The progressive loss of executor slots continues across different DAGs; the stale entries are not limited to tasks using deferrable operators.
N3.label: N3 workload characteristics established

symptoms_visible: With `AIRFLOW__SCHEDULER__NUM_RUNS` set to `100000`, the scheduler loop restarts about every two hours and the progressive scheduling slowdown no longer occurs.
N4.label: N4 terminal resolved by scheduler recycling shortcut

symptoms_visible: With `AIRFLOW__SCHEDULER__NUM_RUNS` set to `100000`, the scheduler loop restarts about every two hours and the progressive scheduling slowdown no longer occurs.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal resolved after configuration validation

solution.intent: Upgrade from Airflow 2.5.3 to the newer 2.6.3 maintenance release and see whether the progressive scheduler slowdown disappears.
solution.concrete_example: Deploy Airflow 2.6.3 to production and monitor it through the usual 2-3 week failure window.

edges.comment: Opening reporter's system only. From c0-c2: the reporter deployed Airflow 2.6.3, but the same gradual executor-slot loss returned, so a version bump alone was falsified.

question_patterns: Can you compare scheduler and task logs for a task left in the executor's running set with another execution of the same task that was removed normally?
When this happens, what state do the affected task instances have when you inspect them, and do their logs differ from normal executions?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We've compared logs from different tasks and from separate executions of the same tasks, but we couldn't spot any oddity. By the time we inspect them, the tasks have completed and are no longer in the database `running` state.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every retained task has a scheduler error immediately before completion, while normal executions do not have that error.
I found no difference after comparing a larger sample of task and scheduler logs.

edges.comment: Reporter c4, answering the log-comparison request in c3. The answer preserves the reporter's raw observation and does not claim which race or executor callback failed.

question_patterns: Do you run deferrable tasks or a triggerer?
Are the retained task instances associated with deferrable operators?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, we have quite a few deferrable tasks. Our triggers run in never-ending loops and poll an HTTP endpoint for messages, with their schedules stacked until they reach `max_active_runs`. However, the tasks that remain in the executor set do not necessarily use deferrable operators.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: All retained entries are the same deferrable operator, and its trigger logs terminate with the same exception every time.
The HTTP endpoint is hosted in a different Kubernetes namespace.

edges.comment: Reporter c4, answering the deferrable-task question from c3. The reporter explicitly says the retained entries are not confined to deferrable operators, so that hypothesis was not established as the cause.

solution.intent: Bound the scheduler process lifetime with `AIRFLOW__SCHEDULER__NUM_RUNS` so accumulated in-memory executor bookkeeping is periodically cleared before stale running entries consume all open slots, then monitor through the normal failure window.
solution.concrete_example: Set `AIRFLOW__SCHEDULER__NUM_RUNS=100000`. In this deployment that restarts the scheduler loop about every two hours. Keep monitoring for the usual 2-3 week period before declaring the problem resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The evidence establishes that completed task-instance keys accumulate in the executor's in-memory running set and that recycling the scheduler clears the condition. It does not establish the later multi-scheduler completed-pod-adoption diagnosis for this reporter's deployment, so that more specific mechanism should not be presented as confirmed here.

edges.comment: Reporter c16-c17: the reporter configured AIRFLOW__SCHEDULER__NUM_RUNS=100000, initially monitored because failure normally took 2-3 weeks, and then explicitly confirmed that it fixed the problem. Later comments propose Kubernetes adoption fixes for other affected deployments, but the original reporter never verified those patches; they are not spliced into this resolution.

solution.intent: Bound the scheduler process lifetime with `AIRFLOW__SCHEDULER__NUM_RUNS` so accumulated in-memory executor bookkeeping is periodically cleared before stale running entries consume all open slots, then monitor through the normal failure window.
solution.concrete_example: Set `AIRFLOW__SCHEDULER__NUM_RUNS=100000`. In this deployment that restarts the scheduler loop about every two hours. Keep monitoring for the usual 2-3 week period before declaring the problem resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The opening evidence already shows stale completed entries accumulating in memory and a scheduler restart restoring capacity. This supports periodic scheduler recycling without requiring the later unsuccessful upgrade and workload-hypothesis checks.

edges.comment: Shortcut copy of the reporter-confirmed workaround for an agent that proposes the correct mitigation immediately. It avoids forcing the real but unsuccessful Airflow 2.6.3 upgrade before accepting the working answer.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the established failure mode: completed task-instance keys accumulate in the executor's in-memory running set, reducing reported open slots until the scheduler stops launching work even though the UI and metadata database show no running tasks.
Must ground the diagnosis in the observed inverse running/open-slot metrics, stale completed entries in `self.running`, and immediate recovery after scheduler restart.

Must recommend bounding the scheduler lifetime with `AIRFLOW__SCHEDULER__NUM_RUNS` or an equivalent periodic scheduler recycle; the reporter-confirmed setting was `100000`, approximately every two hours in this deployment.
Must not present upgrading to Airflow 2.6.3 alone as the fix, because the progressive slowdown returned after that upgrade.
Must not claim that deferrable tasks were proven to be the cause; retained entries also came from tasks without deferrable operators.
Must require monitoring through the deployment's normal 2-3 week failure window before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Airflow platform operator who can deploy production upgrades, inspect scheduler internals, add KubernetesExecutor debug logging, query PostgreSQL task state, and interpret Grafana executor metrics.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, courteous, and evidence-driven; provides code references and raw observations, answers questions inline, and clearly distinguishes confirmed behavior from hypotheses.
